acceptable_risk_candidates.status: Pending user choice; no candidate is active
acceptable_risk_candidates.calibration: Frozen three-year daily unfiltered observations only; not calibrated to the filtered or non-overlapping cohorts.
acceptable_risk_candidates.definition: A stock-exposure proxy: expected maximum closing loss contributed by 3% decline events = event probability × conditional mean event severity. The 25/50/75 bp budgets are hypothetical five-session risk budgets, not estimated alpha or option losses. Dollar examples assume $12,000 underlying exposure, not an actual position.
acceptable_risk_candidates.limitation: These illustrative budgets use daily unfiltered severity, so they do not guarantee the same budget for filtered or non-overlapping samples. Tail severity is uncertain and may increase in stress. The proxy ignores sub-3% losses, intraday moves, option convexity, premium, assignments and portfolio dependence; it cannot set an executable option-risk limit without judgment.

option_economics.status: Dated option-price capability established; comparative alpha still not estimable
option_economics.scope: Nearest observed puts, six per stock, one expiry. Availability sample only: not target-delta selections, actual trades, a matched filtered/unfiltered backtest or an independent sample of profits.
option_economics.payoff_definition: Illustrative net short-put payoff = 100 × (assumed entry bid or midpoint − max(strike − observed expiry stock close, 0)) − $3.30 research cost. Divide by 100 × strike for the collateral yield. This marks an assigned stock purchase to the expiry close; it does not assume the stock was sold or a Wheel cycle completed.
option_economics.assumptions: Ordinary 100-share deliverable research assumption consistent with retained standard-contract descriptions, not an individual historical OCC confirmation. Daily BBO fields do not certify a simultaneous executable closing NBBO. No execution or assignment is inferred.
option_economics.missing: Full dated candidate history, usable historical delta or complete observed-strike fallback candidates, matched strategy arms and capital/idle-cash accounting remain missing. One week cannot estimate expected option alpha.

design.signal: Previous completed XNYS close before scheduled entry; unchanged production indicators.
design.schedule: Entry is the last XNYS session of each calendar week, normally Friday. Hypothetical expiry is the last XNYS session on/before the following Friday.
design.selection: One fixed opportunity per week, not first-passing-day selection or the actual daily order engine.
design.strike: Ratio times previous completed signal close; not a listed strike, entry-time ATM or a 25-delta contract.
design.horizon: Normally 6–8 calendar days; require 3–10. Use actual holiday/early-close calendar; no invented holiday prices.
design.payoff: max(K - expiry stock close, 0) / K; normalized collateral, not option return.
design.costs: Research budget $3.30 per standard 100-share scenario, not a broker quote or production fee change.
design.idle: A rejected opportunity has zero incremental option payoff/cost, NOT a measured zero cash return. No cash yield, equity curve, compounding, reinvestment or portfolio allocation is assumed.
design.bootstrap: Joint non-circular moving blocks of weekly opportunity dates; same indices across all stocks, ratios and nested groups.
design.uncertainty: Approximate pointwise percentile intervals; no multiplicity correction, stationarity or causal guarantee.
design.limitation: Terminal intrinsic only: excludes early exercise, assignment-stock holding, dividends, contract adjustments, market premiums and implied volatility. As-retrieved prices and survivor selection remain limitations.

hypothetical_put_payoff.comparison: Positive differences mean less hypothetical liability/cost, NOT higher returns. Weekly results use matched valid weeks and zero incremental option activity in skipped weeks.
hypothetical_put_payoff.premium_budget: Let q be the selected-week share, B_U and B_F be all/selected conditional break-even rates after cost. Equal expected weekly net cashflow requires q*p_F - p_U = q*B_F - B_U. The allowable weekly forgone premium is B_U - q*B_F. At equal constant premium p in both groups, filtering helps only if p < (B_U - q*B_F)/(1-q), ignoring cash yield. No actual premium or alpha is inferred.
